findings.finding: HUD's 2025 OMB inventory reports only 1-100 users for Microsoft Copilot across every general-purpose task; no public source documents an agency-wide AI rollout or a larger seat count.
findings.notes: Follow-up coverage of HUD (omitted from the original four research batches). Checked hud.gov/ai and searched FedScoop / Nextgov / GovExec for a HUD Microsoft Copilot or general-purpose chat rollout; the hud.gov/ai page carries no employee-access numbers, seat counts, or agency-wide-availability language. The only signal of scale is the OMB 2025 inventory itself, which reports the 1-100 bucket for Microsoft Copilot on all four general-purpose tasks (drafting, written communications, knowledge retrieval, word processors) — i.e. a small pilot against a ~8,000-person workforce. HUD's most prominently covered AI effort in the press is a proposed case-summary / suggested-email-response tool that drew objections from EPIC and the Center for Democracy & Technology; that is a task-specific system, not general-purpose employee AI access. No verified deployment-scale source exists for HUD.
